text:
Maria Chen: FYI — escalated from Support: customer acme-inc on Dedicated cluster rdx-us-west-2-2 reports sudden throughput collapse starting ~02:00 UTC. p50 OK, but p95/p99 spiked and we're seeing 429s + many timeouts. Billing shows tokens/min dropped while infra costs spiked. attaching quick logs below.

Ajay Patel: Can you paste the request samples and the 429 body? Also which model and route?

Maria Chen: route=/v1/generate model=gpt-open-16k-quantized. Sample 429: 
```json
{"error":"throttled","code":429,"message":"exceeded throughput quota on node"}
```
Payloads are tiny (avg 10 tokens), high QPS (~1.2k rps).

support-bot: Alert: billing-anomaly for acme-inc — spike in GPU hours between 01:45-02:15 UTC. (link to ticket #INC-3241)

Liam O'Neill: This smells like inefficient batching + scheduler thrash. Small prompts + aggressive low batch_window forces many tiny batches, GPU context-switch overhead kills throughput. Any recent config changes on that cluster?

Maria Chen: Ops says a config change rolled 2 days ago to reduce latency for low-latency customers: batch_window_ms from 50 -> 5 on that pool. Also enabled continuous batching experiment.

Ajay Patel: That matches. If batch_window_ms is too low with many short requests, we end up with thousands of tiny batches. Also autoscaler can misread utilization and scale wrong. Can we fetch per-node batching metrics?

Olga Sokolova: Pulling metrics now. Command I used: 
```
redwoodctl metrics query --cluster rdx-us-west-2-2 --name batching.* --range 15m
```
Prelim: batch_count/sec spiked x12, avg batch_size dropped from 28->6, GPU utilization dropped from 82%->47, context-switch ops increased.

Liam O'Neill: Exactly. Max_batch_size seems to be 32 but average batch size << that because batch_window_ms too low. Combined with continuous batching prefill behavior, scheduler is dispatching earlier. Also saw one tenant with long-running outputs (~3k tokens) pinned to same device — possible noisy neighbor.

Maria Chen: Customer timeline: 01:40 normal; 01:50 we turned on canary config; 02:00 customer calls. Ops history shows a single tenant (acme-analytics) started a large job at 01:55 on same pool.

Ajay Patel: Two-pronged problem: (1) config shifted batch timing causing small batches, (2) noisy neighbor producing long decode workloads occupying queue slots. Immediate mitigation: revert batch_window to 50ms on canary nodes, set per-tenant concurrency cap, and enable batch aggregation by token (max_batch_tokens).

Olga Sokolova: I can patch canary node now. Proposed quick patch: 
```yaml
batching:
  batch_window_ms: 50
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  continuous_batching: enabled
scheduler:
  policy: token_aware
  tenant_shares: true
```
Applying to one node in pool rdx-us-west-2-2-canary-3.

runtime-oncall: Patch applied to canary node at 02:05 UTC. Rolling metrics...

runtime-oncall: Observed after change: avg batch_size increased 6->30, batches/sec down 12x, GPU utilization jumped 47%->78%, p99 latency improved by ~400ms. Noisy tenant still present but less blocking.

Maria Chen: Can we repro the issue locally so SRE & Support can provide deterministic repro steps to the customer? Need commands to share.

Liam O'Neill: Repro script (synthetic): use 1k concurrent clients sending 10-token prompts at 1.2k rps against dedicated pool, then start a long-output job (3k tokens) on a single node and watch throughput. Example using wrk: 
```
wrk -t64 -c1000 -d60s -s scripts/post-small.lua --latency http://rdx-canary.internal/v1/generate
```
post-small.lua will send minimal JSON payloads. Then run a long-run decoder job: 
```
curl -X POST http://rdx-node.internal/long-run -d '{"prompt":"<<long prompt>>","max_tokens":3000}'
```
Expect to see avg batch_size collapse and 429s appear.

Ajay Patel: Long-term fixes: per-tenant isolation (cgroups on scheduler), token-aware scheduling, adaptive batch_window that increases under high fan-out, and autoscaler hysteresis so it doesn't thrash on transient load. Also add a health gauge: "effective_tokens_per_sec" per node.

Maria Chen: I've updated the support ticket with mitigation steps & notified acme-inc that we're applying canary rollback. Customer impact window ~15 min.

Olga Sokolova: Will schedule a follow-up to roll config cluster-wide if canary stays green for 30m. Adding an alert rule: if avg_batch_size < 10 AND batches/sec > 500 -> paged to runtime oncall.

runtime-oncall: Added alert, increased autoscaler cooldown to 5m (was 30s) for this pool. Monitoring for thrash.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — marking this thread for postmortem. We'll include config diff and repro steps. :thumbsup:
